Pike: Long duck-bill snout, pale bean markings, posterior dorsal and forked tail visible. Narrow left/right framing.
Bass: Large mouth, dark lateral band and distinct spiny/soft dorsal outline visible. Narrow left/right framing.
Char: Pale spots on dark flank, orange underside, light fin edges and separate adipose visible. Narrow left/right framing.
Sturgeon: Pointed snout, ventral barbels, repeated raised scutes and asymmetric caudal visible. Narrow left/right framing; scute arrangement requires independent anatomy review.
Paddlefish: Long flattened rostrum and wide open mouth visible. Posterior fin shapes and paired-fin overlap need author review. Narrow right margin.
Arowana: Large ordered scales, upturned mouth, two barbels and long posterior fins visible. Full tail visible; ample upper/lower margins.
Arapaima: Large dark scales with red rear edges and rounded caudal visible. Complete fin roots visible; lateral margins need measurement.
Goldfish: Orange/white scales, deep body and long divided flowing caudal visible. Fancy form rather than streamlined wild form; fins overlap near roots.
Swift: Dark swept folded wing, pale throat, tiny bill with broad open gape and two short legs visible. Long wing tips overlap the tail silhouette; tail identity requires ownership review.
Swallow: Blue back, reddish throat, pale underside and long forked tail streamers visible. Wing is folded above tail, two feet separate.
Falcon: Dark malar moustache below eye, hooked bill, streaked pale underside visible. Folded wings sit above banded tail; two separate feet.
Crane: Red crown, long bill/neck and two separated long legs visible. Drooping rear feather plumes obscure a clean tail boundary; ownership review needed.
Spoonbill: Broad spatulate bill and long legs visible. Pink/white coat rather than purely white; folded wing partly obscures short tail boundary.
Kestrel: Hooked bill with dark moustache stripe and black-spotted rufous back visible. Banded tail below folded wings; two separated feet.
Guineafowl: Dense white spots, bare blue/red head and casque visible. Folded wing above short tail; two separated feet.
Pheasant: Ringed neck, red face, patterned flank and long barred tapered tail visible. Tail root partly obscured by wing feathers; two separate feet.
Capybara: Blunt muzzle, small rounded ears and barrel body visible. Four separate feet, no visible tail; near/far limbs still overlap at roots. Standing rather than strong stride.
Agouti: Grizzled orange-brown fur, rounded ears and tall rump visible. Four distinct feet but rear roots overlap, tail not independently resolved. Standing rather than strong stride.
Alpaca: Short face, straight pointed ears and woolly coat visible. Four separate feet and short full tail; upper limbs obscured by fleece. Standing rather than strong stride.
Llama: Longer face, curved upright ears and full short tail visible. Four feet separate but proximal limbs overlap under fleece. Standing rather than strong stride.
Musk Ox: Shaggy skirt, heavy paired horns and four separated feet visible. Head turns slightly toward viewer, tail merges with long rump hair; standing rather than stride.
Pangolin: Overlapping scales, pointed snout and long complete tapering tail visible. Four clawed feet separate; far front attachment needs author review. Lateral margins narrow.
Peccary: Coarse grizzled coat and pale shoulder collar visible; four separate feet. A large exposed downward tusk was generated and needs species-identity review. Tail unresolved; standing rather than stride.
Okapi: Horizontal white stripes on hindquarters and upper legs clearly visible, pale lower legs, short horns and full tufted tail. Four feet separate; near/far roots overlap. Standing rather than stride.
